draft.title: Hypothetical Inference Speed: 18 vs 24 t/s - What's Missing?
draft.body: Exploring a hypothetical local inference scenario, we observed two configurations yielding 18 and 24 tokens per second (t/s) on the same hardware using a single prompt. While these figures provide a baseline, they represent only a partial picture of performance. It's crucial to note that this hypothetical test did not measure the time to first token (TTFT) or assess the quality of the generated answers. A faster raw t/s doesn't guarantee a better user experience if the initial response is delayed or the output requires significant correction. Furthermore, this specific comparison on one prompt shouldn't be interpreted as a definitive conclusion about which configuration is universally superior. Performance can fluctuate based on prompt complexity, system load, and the specific model architecture. This synthetic data aims to highlight the limitations of relying solely on t/s metrics.

draft.title: Beyond Tokens/Second: Analyzing Hypothetical Local LLM Inference
draft.body: This post examines a hypothetical local LLM inference test where two setups achieved 18 and 24 tokens per second (t/s) respectively. The test was conducted on the same machine using a single, specific prompt. It is important to emphasize that these are hypothetical results and do not represent measured outcomes or personal experience. Key metrics such as time to first token (TTFT) and the qualitative aspects of the generated answers were not evaluated in this hypothetical scenario. Therefore, while the t/s figures offer a comparative data point, they do not fully capture the perceived responsiveness or utility of the models. The results from this single prompt test should not be generalized to establish a definitive winner, as performance can vary significantly across different tasks and conditions. The intention here is to discuss the limitations of raw speed metrics.

draft.title: Hypothetical Inference Speeds (18 & 24 t/s): What Metrics Are We Missing?
draft.body: We're analyzing a hypothetical local inference scenario involving two configurations that produced 18 and 24 tokens per second (t/s) on identical hardware with a single prompt. While these speeds are a starting point, they don't tell the whole story. This hypothetical experiment explicitly did not measure critical factors like time to first token (TTFT) or the quality of the output. A model might be fast in terms of t/s but feel slow if it takes a long time to start generating text, or if the generated text is inaccurate and requires re-prompting. Furthermore, as this was a test with one prompt on one machine, it cannot establish a universal performance winner. Different prompts, system loads, and model architectures could yield different results. These hypothetical numbers serve to illustrate that raw t/s is just one piece of the puzzle.

draft.title: Hypothetical Local Inference Speed: Beyond Raw Tokens/Second
draft.body: This post discusses a hypothetical local inference scenario involving two configurations, achieving 18 and 24 tokens per second (t/s) respectively on the same machine with a single prompt. While these numbers offer a basic performance indicator, they represent only one facet of practical usability. Crucially, this hypothetical test did not measure time to first token (TTFT) or the quality of the generated answers. A model with higher t/s might still feel sluggish if TTFT is high, or if the output requires significant revision due to poor quality. Furthermore, the observed difference does not establish a universal winner; performance can vary greatly with different prompts, system loads, and model architectures. These synthetic figures are intended to highlight the limitations of raw t/s metrics and prompt a discussion on what other factors users consider essential for a responsive local LLM experience.
